title: Stability of a simple root under coefficient perturbation over a henselian valued field
statement: Let $F$ be a field with a nontrivial valuation and henselian valuation ring [def-trf-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Its valuation topology has balls $v(x-a)>\gamma$ as a basis, for the additive valuation into a totally ordered abelian group. Let $f(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}c_iT^i\in F[T]$ be monic of degree $n\geq1$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Suppose $a\in F$ is a simple root: $f(a)=0$ and $f^{\prime}(a)\ne0$, where $f^{\prime}$ is the formal derivative. For every open neighbourhood $U$ of $a$ there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $(c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1})$ in the product topology on $F^n$ such that, for every $(d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1})\in V$, the polynomial $g(T)=T^n+\sum_{i<n}d_iT^i$ has a simple root $b\in U$. The valuation may have arbitrary rank; completeness is not assumed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: Write $v(0)=+\infty$. If $\{0\}$ is open, the topology of $F$ is discrete, and $V=\{(c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1})\}$ works with $b=a$. Otherwise every ball about zero contains a nonzero element: for every bound $\lambda$ we can choose $t\ne0$ with $v(t)>\lambda$. Put $R=\{x:v(x)\geq0\}$ and $\mathfrak m=\{x:v(x)>0\}$. The valuation inequalities show that $R$ is a subring and $\mathfrak m$ an ideal; an element of $R$ outside $\mathfrak m$ has valuation zero and its inverse lies in $R$, whereas an element of $\mathfrak m$ cannot be a unit. Thus $R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and is the assumed henselian valuation ring. The fraction-field valuation-ring property follows since either $v(x)\geq0$ or $v(x^{-1})>0$ for $x\ne0$.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: Choose $\gamma$ such that $\{x:v(x-a)>\gamma\}\subseteq U$. Set $c_n=1$ and expand, by the binomial formula, $f(a+Z)=\sum_{j=0}^n A_jZ^j$, with $A_j=\sum_{i=j}^n\binom{i}{j}c_i a^{i-j}$. Then $A_0=0$ and $A_1=e=f^{\prime}(a)\ne0$. Choose nonzero $t$ with $\delta=v(t)>\max(0,\gamma)$ and $\delta>v(e)-v(A_j)$ for every nonzero $A_j$ with $2\leq j\leq n$. This is possible by the preceding ball observation and finiteness. Consequently $v(A_j)+(j-1)\delta-v(e)>0$ for all $j\geq2$ with $A_j\ne0$. No multiples of a fixed positive value are asserted to be cofinal.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: For a coefficient tuple $d$, set $d_n=1$ and $B_j(d)=\sum_{i=j}^n\binom{i}{j}d_i a^{i-j}$. Put $\theta_j=v(e)-(j-1)\delta$ for $0\leq j\leq n$ (so $\theta_0=v(te)$). Choose $\beta$ strictly larger than all bounds $\theta_j-v(\binom{i}{j}a^{i-j})$ for nonzero multipliers with $0\leq j\leq i<n$. Such a bound exists because the list is finite and the nontrivial valuation provides a positive value to add to its maximum. Let $V$ be the product of the open balls $v(d_i-c_i)>\beta$. Since $B_j(d)-A_j=\sum_{i=j}^{n-1}\binom{i}{j}(d_i-c_i)a^{i-j}$, the valuation inequality for a finite sum gives $v(B_j(d)-A_j)>\theta_j$ for every $j$, including empty sums. This proves the required uniform coefficient control directly.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: Fix $d\in V$ and its polynomial $g$. Define $h(X)=g(a+tX)/(te)=\sum_{j=0}^n h_jX^j$, where $h_j=B_j(d)t^{j-1}/e$. The preceding inequalities give $h_0\in\mathfrak m$, $h_1-1\in\mathfrak m$ and $h_j\in\mathfrak m$ for $j\geq2$: for the last assertion apply the valuation inequality to $B_j=A_j+(B_j-A_j)$ and use the bound on $A_j$ from step 2. Hence $h\in R[X]$ and $\overline h=X$. Its degree is $n$, since its leading coefficient is $t^{n-1}/e\ne0$.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: The polynomial $h$ need not be monic, so form the explicit polynomial $Q(Y)=h(1)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^n h_jY^{n-j}(Y+1)^j\in R[Y]$. Here $h(1)\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m}$ is a unit. The coefficient of $Y^n$ is $h(1)^{-1}\sum_jh_j=1$, so $Q$ is monic. Reducing the displayed expression gives $\overline Q=Y^{n-1}(Y+1)$. Therefore $-1$ is a residue root and $\overline Q^{\prime}(-1)=(-1)^{n-1}\ne0$, also when $n=1$ or the residue characteristic is two.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting], implication (i) to (ii), to the henselian local ring $R$, the monic polynomial $Q$, and the simple residue root $-1$. It gives $y\in R$ with $Q(y)=0$ and $\overline y=-1$. Thus $y$ is a unit, $z=1+y^{-1}\in\mathfrak m$, and the defining expression for $Q$ gives $0=Q(y)=h(1)^{-1}y^nh(1+y^{-1})$. Both factors outside $h$ are units, whence $h(z)=0$.

source.place: Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), monic simple-root criterion; agent-written valuation rescaling and reciprocal-polynomial argument for the topological application in ILO XX 4.4, printed p.374.

proof.text: Put $b=a+tz$. The identity defining $h$ gives $g(b)=teh(z)=0$, and $v(b-a)=\delta+v(z)>\gamma$ (with $v(0)=+\infty$), so $b\in U$. Since $\overline h=X$ and $z\in\mathfrak m$, reducing the derivative evaluation gives $\overline{h^{\prime}(z)}=1$; in particular $h^{\prime}(z)\ne0$. Differentiating the finite polynomial identity $h(X)=g(a+tX)/(te)$ term by term yields $h^{\prime}(X)=g^{\prime}(a+tX)/e$. Hence $g^{\prime}(b)=e h^{\prime}(z)\ne0$, so $b$ is simple. All constructions used finite sums and ordered-group inequalities, with no completeness or rank hypothesis.
